  coordinator_prior_engagement: >-

    matched the prior most closely; finding a different mechanism and a wider

  joint_J2:
    title: STAGE C CERTIFICATE ROUTE - certificate route + halving-induction soundness
    verdict: DISSENT
    verdict_scope: >-
      Scoped dissent: the certificate route AS DOCUMENTED is not yet sound
      for every case the document itself uses it for. Neither finding below
      threatens the PRIMARY claim path on curve 302 itself (trivial torsion,
      Stage-0-established) once the identified defects are fixed; both
      threaten claims the document makes about material this joint was
      assigned to check (the resolvent-cubic prime-set argument, and the
      nonzero-torsion controls' theoretical backing).
    finding_1_resolvent_cubic_identity:
      severity: moderate, harmless-in-effect-for-curve-302
      claim_attacked: >-
        search_boundary.stage_a_selmer_computation.tracked_object and
        idea.claim both assert "Delta_E = 16*disc(resolvent cubic of the
        short-Weierstrass form)" and call it "a standard identity", using it
        to argue the resolvent cubic "introduces no new primes of Q beyond
        bad_primes(Delta_E)" -- the load-bearing basis for Stage A's frozen
        prime set S. Review-plan J2 attack_plan item (1) explicitly assigns
        checking this identity by hand for a curve with a1, a3 nonzero
        (curve 302 has a1=a2=a3=1), which is what follows.
      hand_derivation: >-
        Standard facts (Silverman AEC III.1, recalled): for ainvs
        (a1,a2,a3,a4,a6), b2=a1^2+4a2, b4=2a4+a1a3, b6=a3^2+4a6,
        c4=b2^2-24b4, c6=-b2^3+36b2b4-216b6, and the polynomial identity
        1728*Delta = c4^3 - c6^2 (always true, independent of the model).
        There are TWO materially different ways to reach a short Weierstrass
        form y^2=x^3+A*x+B from a general model with a1,a3 != 0, and the
        document (baseline_reproduction.short_weierstrass_conversion.method)
        itself names both without choosing between them: "A, B exact
        rationals (or, after clearing denominators, integers up to a fixed
        scaling)".
        (a) TRANSLATION-ONLY (u=1, A,B left as exact rationals): complete the
        square via y' = y + (a1*x+a3)/2 (no scaling, only a shift), then the
        cube via x' = x + b2/12 (again a pure shift). This changes NO
        coordinate by a scale factor, so it leaves Delta EXACTLY invariant.
        For this h(t)=t^3+A*t+B, disc(h) = -4A^3-27B^2, and since this is the
        SAME curve just translated, disc(h) = Delta/16 exactly (equivalently
        Delta = 16*disc(h)) -- i.e. in THIS reading the document's identity
        is exactly correct.
        (b) STANDARD c4,c6-SCALED FORM (the form actually printed in most
        references and used to get an INTEGRAL model): A=-27*c4, B=-54*c6.
        Then disc(h) = -4A^3-27B^2 = -4*(-27c4)^3 - 27*(-54c6)^2 =
        78732*c4^3 - 78732*c6^2 = 78732*(c4^3-c6^2) = 78732*1728*Delta.
        Factoring: 78732 = 2^2*3^9, 1728 = 2^6*3^3, so
        78732*1728 = 2^8*3^12 = 136,048,896. So disc(h) = 2^8*3^12*Delta in
        THIS reading -- Delta = disc(h)/16 is off by a factor of 2^8*3^12,
        NOT the "16*" relation the document states.
        Conclusion: the identity "Delta_E = 16*disc(resolvent cubic)" is
        exactly true under reading (a) and FALSE by a huge, specific factor
        under reading (b); the document does not commit to which reading it
        means when it calls this "a standard identity" in search_boundary
        and idea.claim, even though baseline_reproduction's OWN text
        correctly flags that "this transformation and its effect on Delta by
        an explicit power of the scaling unit are RE-DERIVED SYMBOLICALLY at
        Stage 0... not asserted here as a specific numeric formula, to avoid
        a load-bearing recalled constant." search_boundary does exactly what
        baseline_reproduction warns against: it asserts the specific numeric
        constant (16x) as settled, in a load-bearing spot, without the
        scaling-unit caveat.
      practical_consequence_for_curve_302: >-
        Harmless in effect, disclosed rather than hidden: under reading (b)
        (the more standard, integral-model convention), the only "new"
        primes the 2^8*3^12 factor could contribute are 2 and 3, and curve
        302's frozen bad_primes list already contains both ("2","3" are the
        first two entries). So whichever reading Stage 0 actually implements,
        S = {2} union {primes dividing Delta(E)} remains exhaustive for THIS
        curve -- the prime-set argument's CONCLUSION survives, but not
        because the cited identity is correct as stated; it survives by a
        curve-specific coincidence the document does not name.
      required_change: >-
        Replace "a standard identity" with the exact identity for whichever
        conversion convention Stage 0 actually adopts (translation-only:
        Delta=16*disc(h) exactly; scaled/integral: disc(h)=2^8*3^12*Delta),
        and add an explicit Stage-0 sub-check that any primes introduced by
        the chosen scaling (2 and 3, under the scaled convention) are already
        members of bad_primes(Delta_E) before relying on S's exhaustiveness --
        this happens to hold for curve 302 but is not proven to hold in
        general, and the protocol's own language ("a standard identity")
        implies a generality it has not demonstrated.
    finding_2_halving_induction_scope_gap:
      severity: substantive, primary finding
      claim_attacked: >-
        certificate_route.matrix_rank_implies_independence_proof, advertised
        as "SELF-CONTAINED, RE-DERIVED HERE RATHER THAN IMPORTED
        UNCRITICALLY", and used throughout the document (including by
        controls.nearby_object_control and
        controls.rational_2_torsion_applicability) to justify
        "matrixRank - torsionRank = n implies Z-independence of n points
        modulo torsion" for ANY curve, torsion-trivial or not.
      hand_derivation_of_the_given_proof: >-
        Re-derived step by step. Ψ: E(Q) -> direct-sum over p in S' of
        E(F_p)/2E(F_p) is a composite of the reduction homomorphism
        E(Q)->E(F_p) (a group homomorphism at any prime of good reduction,
        standard fact) and the quotient map to E(F_p)/2E(F_p); since the
        target has exponent 2, Ψ(2P)=0 for all P, so Ψ factors through
        E(Q)/2E(Q). Given Sigma(a_i*P_i)=O with a minimal counterexample
        M=max|a_i|>0: applying Ψ gives Sigma(a_i mod 2)*row_i = 0 in the F2
        target. If some a_i is odd, this is a NONTRIVIAL F2 relation among
        the rows (the vector (a_i mod 2) is nonzero), contradicting the rows
        being linearly independent (matrixRank=n, full rank). So every a_i
        is even, a_i=2*b_i; Sigma(b_i*P_i) is directly computable via the
        rational group law (no existence question), and
        2*Sigma(b_i*P_i)=Sigma(a_i*P_i)=O, so Sigma(b_i*P_i) is in E(Q)[2].
        THIS IS WHERE THE PROOF USES TRIVIAL TORSION: it concludes
        Sigma(b_i*P_i)=O because E(Q)_tors={O} (Stage 0), giving a strictly
        smaller relation with the SAME points, contradicting minimality of M.
        I find NO flaw in this chain for the case it is actually stated for
        (E(Q)_tors={O}): the odd/even split, the homomorphism property, and
        the descent termination (well-founded on max|a_i| in Z) are all
        correct and standard. This is the part the coordinator's prior
        expected to break (a "parity gap"); it does not break here.
      the_actual_gap: >-
        The proof's opening line is explicit: "Suppose Sigma(a_i*Pi) = O
        (TORSION IS TRIVIAL, SO ANY RELATION REDUCES TO THE IDENTITY)" --
        this hypothesis is BAKED INTO the setup, not a side remark. For a
        curve with nontrivial torsion (as controls.nearby_object_control and
        controls.rational_2_torsion_applicability explicitly require: "a
        curve WITH nontrivial rational torsion... plus the torsion
        generator"), a Z-relation among points need not reduce to O; it
        reduces to Sigma(a_i*P_i) = T for T ranging over E(Q)_tors, and the
        step "Sigma(b_i*P_i) is in E(Q)[2], hence O" fails outright -- it is
        only in E(Q)[2], which for a torsion-bearing curve is NOT trivial,
        so the descent does not automatically terminate at the zero relation;
        the argument would need to be re-run in the quotient E(Q)/E(Q)_tors
        (or equivalently track torsion-generator rows through the SAME mod-2
        argument) to reach the general "matrixRank - torsionRank = n"
        conclusion, and the document supplies NONE of that extension. It
        supplies torsion_rows (adding rows for a torsion generator) and
        asserts torsion_row_rank is "computed as the F2-rank of the
        torsion-generated subspace", but nowhere re-derives why subtracting
        that rank from matrixRank is exactly the right correction --
        it is stated as a definition/recipe, not proved from the given
        induction, which explicitly excludes this case in its own first
        sentence.
      why_this_matters: >-
        This is precisely the review-plan's requested breaking_artifact: "a
        specific unstated precondition of the halving induction." The
        precondition is: E(Q)_tors = {O}. The document calls the proof
        "self-contained" while using its conclusion (matrixRank -
        torsionRank = n, in general) for curves the proof's own hypothesis
        excludes. This does NOT threaten curve 302's own Stage-C certificate
        (trivial torsion, in scope of the proof as literally written), but it
        DOES mean two of the document's own required controls
        (nearby_object_control, rational_2_torsion_applicability) rest on an
        unproven generalization of the very theorem those controls exist to
        stress-test -- see joint J3 and proves_too_much object 2 below.
      required_change: >-
        Either (a) supply the general proof (working in E(Q)/E(Q)_tors, or
        extending the mod-2 argument to explicitly carry torsion-generator
        rows through the same minimal-counterexample logic), or (b) restrict
        the document's claimed theorem to torsion-trivial curves only and
        state PLAINLY that the nonzero-torsion controls' "expected_outcome"
        is a design-time PREDICTION pending that separate proof, not a
        corollary of the proof actually given.
    finding_3_reduction_map_precondition:
      severity: minor, non-fatal
      claim_attacked: certificate_route.reduction_map / good_primes_and_preconditions
      hand_derivation: >-
        For a prime p of good reduction, the reduction map E(Q)->E(F_p) is
        classically defined on ALL of E(Q) via projective coordinates: a
        point whose affine x-coordinate has p in its denominator reduces
        (correctly, as a group homomorphism) to O in E(F_p), not to an
        "undefined" value. The document instead treats such (point, prime)
        pairs as failures of a stated precondition ("requiring p not divide
        either coordinate's denominator... which (point, prime) pairs were
        skipped... extending S' with an additional prime"), which is an
        operationally different (and unnecessarily lossy) convention: the
        mathematically correct row entry there is simply the zero vector for
        that prime's block, not a skip.
      practical_consequence: >-
        Not fatal: since each of the finitely many points has only finitely
        many denominator primes, and the good-prime candidates are unbounded,
        S' can always be extended to route around every collision, so the
        WORKAROUND achieves the same practical effect as the correct
        convention for a fixed, finite point set. But the document should
        say this (a completeness argument: only finitely many exclusions per
        point, infinitely many candidate primes, so extension always
        succeeds) rather than leaving "how that was handled" as an ad hoc,
        unproven per-run decision.
      required_change: >-
        State either the correct reduce-to-O convention (preferred, avoids
        the workaround entirely) or the finite-exclusion completeness
        argument for why extending S' is always sufficient.

  joint_J3:
    title: CONTROLS ADEQUACY
    verdict: DISSENT
    sibling_question_method: >-
      Per the attack plan: for each control, "would this control PASS even
      if the property it claims to isolate were violated?" Applied to all
      five controls below.
    finding_1_no_ascent_control_exists:
      severity: substantive, primary finding
      analysis: >-
        Enumerate the five controls' predicted outcomes: null_control
        (rank STAYS at 31), P32=P1+P2 (rank STAYS at 31), P32=2*P1 (rank
        STAYS at 31), positive_control (rank equals a SEPARATE, unrelated
        curve's own known rank -- not a test of curve 302's own pipeline
        instance detecting a NEW point), nearby_object_control (rank equals a
        SEPARATE curve's small declared count, again not curve 302's
        pipeline). Every one of these is a "stays the same or matches a
        DIFFERENT curve's already-known value" test. NONE of them is a test
        of the one behavior Stage C must actually exhibit if Stage B ever
        succeeds: given curve 302's own 31-point basis PLUS a KNOWN,
        independently verified Z-INDEPENDENT 32nd point (at a comparable
        coordinate/height scale), does the pipeline correctly ASCEND
        matrixRank to 32? Sibling-question test applied to null_control
        specifically: null_control would PASS (rank stays 31) under the
        CORRECT implementation, but it would ALSO pass under a completely
        broken implementation that is simply incapable of ever reporting
        rank > 31 for ANY 32nd point -- e.g. because the good-prime list S'
        selection procedure or the F2 character-basis dimension is
        systematically insufficient at curve 302's actual coordinate scale
        (naive height up to ~468, per the frozen JSON, and the document's own
        interpretation_limits already flag this scale as a source of low
        power for Stage B; the identical scale risk applies to Stage C's
        reduction map, which is never stress-tested at this scale by any
        control). The null control's PASS signature is therefore
        INDISTINGUISHABLE between "correctly detects the duplicate row" and
        "cannot detect independence at all, at any input." This exact
        argument extends to BOTH proves_too_much controls (they too only test
        "stays at 31") and to positive_control / nearby_object_control (they
        test ascent, but on curves and point sets that are NOT curve 302 and
        are not disclosed to be at a comparable coordinate/height scale, so a
        pass there does not certify that the SAME pipeline instance,
        configured for curve 302's actual denominators and prime list, can
        ascend).
      missing_sibling_control: >-
        A control using a KNOWN, independently documented, GENUINELY
        Z-independent point ADDED to an already-certified basis, at a
        comparable scale to the target case, expecting matrixRank -
        torsionRank to correctly ASCEND to the new higher value. Concretely:
        extend positive_control's own rank-r curve with one more
        independently verified generator to rank r+1 (a small, well-known
        curve where an (r+1)-th generator is independently documented, e.g.
        an LMFDB curve one rank higher than whatever positive_control settles
        on), and require the pipeline to report exactly r+1, not r. Without
        this, the coordinator's own stated worry ("the null control... [is]
        weak evidence of independence sensitivity") is CONFIRMED and shown to
        extend to the entire control suite, not just the null control.
      breaking_artifact_named: >-
        A degenerate certificate-route implementation that always reports
        matrixRank = (number of points in the frozen 31-point baseline) and
        NEVER increases regardless of what is appended -- e.g. a bug that
        caps the F2 matrix's column dimension at whatever was needed for the
        31-point Stage-0 reproduction and silently truncates or ignores rows
        beyond that -- would PASS Stage 0's own rank31_baseline_certificate
        (31 points -> rank 31, correct), PASS null_control (32nd row
        duplicate or not, rank stays "31" either way), PASS both
        proves_too_much controls (same reason), and PASS positive_control /
        nearby_object_control if those are run on entirely separate smaller
        problem instances not sharing this bug's trigger condition. It would
        then FAIL SILENTLY -- reporting "not independent" -- on a genuine
        Stage-B witness, which is exactly the single most consequential
        wrong answer this protocol can produce (a false negative on a real
        discovery), and no control in the current suite would have caught it
        before that point.
    finding_2_deferred_concrete_curves_compound_finding_1:
      severity: minor, disclosed
      analysis: >-
        positive_control and nearby_object_control both explicitly defer
        their exact curve and generators to a future Stage-0 sub-task ("not
        asserted here"). This is disclosed, not hidden, so it is not treated
        as an independent adequacy failure. But it compounds finding 1:
        because no concrete curve is named yet, no one has checked whether
        either control's points will be anywhere near curve 302's own
        coordinate/height scale (~468 in natural-log units) -- so even once
        instantiated, these controls may continue to exercise a much easier
        regime than the one Stage C must actually perform in, leaving the
        ascent gap in finding 1 unaddressed by controls as currently
        specified.
    finding_3_null_control_arithmetic_is_correctly_forced:
      severity: none (confirms design, not a defect)
      hand_derivation: >-
        Independently re-verified: phi maps into an F2-vector space, so
        every nonzero element equals its own inverse (order divides 2);
        therefore Ψ(-P) = -Ψ(P) = Ψ(P) identically, with no dependence on P
        or the specific reduction primes chosen. Row 32 (for Q=-P1) is
        therefore LITERALLY the same vector as row 1, not merely "expected"
        to be -- this holds by the group-theoretic structure of the target
        alone and needs no computation to verify for this specific curve.
        This part of the design is correctly and exactly reasoned; my
        dissent above is about what the control's outcome can and cannot
        distinguish, not about whether the stated arithmetic is right.

  proves_too_much_analysis:
    object_1_null_certificate:
      description: 31 frozen points plus Q=-P1; true independence count 31.
      verdict: CONCUR
      analysis: >-
        Identical object to the protocol's own null_control (see J3 finding
        3). The predicted failure signature (route must report 31, not 32)
        is FORCED by the group-homomorphism structure of Ψ into an F2-vector
        space (Ψ(-P)=Ψ(P) always), independent of any implementation detail
        beyond correctness of the reduction map itself. If implemented as
        specified, this object cannot slip through: I find no configuration
        under which the design, correctly implemented, would report 32 here.
        This is the one place in the whole certificate route where the
        design-level guarantee is airtight rather than merely plausible.
    object_2_full_2_torsion_curve:
      description: >-
        Rank-0 curve with full rational 2-torsion, e.g. y^2 = x^3 - x (true
        torsion 2-rank 2, true independent-point count 0); a route reporting
        torsionRank=0 or a rank of 3 from three "independent" rows overcounts.
      verdict: DISSENT
      hand_derivation: >-
        E: y^2=x^3-x has rational 2-torsion points (0,0), (1,0), (-1,0) with
        (-1,0)=(0,0)+(1,0); E(Q)_tors is the Klein four-group (Z/2)^2,
        generated by (0,0) and (1,0) (standard, recalled fact -- this is a
        well-known CM curve, conductor 32). Reduction mod an odd prime p of
        good reduction is injective on prime-to-p torsion (Silverman AEC
        VII.3.1, recalled), so for p odd and good, (0,0) and (1,0) reduce to
        two DISTINCT nonzero 2-torsion points of E(F_p). A naive
        implementation that computes matrixRank of the two-row matrix from
        these torsion generators WITHOUT subtracting torsionRank would, for
        any p where these two reduced points' images in E(F_p)/2E(F_p) are
        F2-linearly independent (generic behavior, though not asserted here
        as guaranteed for every specific small p), report matrixRank=2 and
        (with torsionRank naively left at 0) overclaim rank 2 where the true
        rank is 0 -- exactly the review-plan's own named failure signature.
        The protocol's nearby_object_control / rational_2_torsion_applicability
        is well-aimed at this exact failure mode IN PRINCIPLE. However, per
        J2 finding 2, the document's OWN proof of "matrixRank - torsionRank
        = n implies independence" is derived ONLY for E(Q)_tors={O}; it does
        not establish, and no other part of the document establishes, that
        subtracting torsionRank is the mathematically CORRECT correction for
        a curve with nontrivial torsion (as opposed to a plausible recipe).
        So the design-level guarantee that the route "must FAIL (report the
        true, smaller number) on this object" is not yet PROVEN by anything
        in this document -- it is asserted by definition/recipe
        (controls.nearby_object_control.expected_outcome) without the

        is exactly correct.

        references and used to get an INTEGRAL model): A=-27*c4, B=-54*c6.

        E(F_p)/2E(F_p) is a composite of the reduction homomorphism
        E(Q)->E(F_p) (a group homomorphism at any prime of good reduction,
        standard fact) and the quotient map to E(F_p)/2E(F_p); since the
        target has exponent 2, Psi(2P)=0 for all P, so Psi factors through

        curve with nontrivial torsion (as controls.nearby_object_control and
        controls.rational_2_torsion_applicability explicitly require: "a
        curve WITH nontrivial rational torsion... plus the torsion
        generator"), a Z-relation among points need not reduce to O; it

        step "Sigma(b_i*P_i) is in E(Q)[2], hence O" fails outright -- it is

        therefore Psi(-P) = -Psi(P) = Psi(P) identically, with no dependence
        on P or the specific reduction primes chosen. Row 32 (for Q=-P1) is
        therefore LITERALLY the same vector as row 1, not merely "expected"
        to be -- this holds by the group-theoretic structure of the target
        alone and needs no computation to verify for this specific curve.
        This part of the design is correctly and exactly reasoned; my
        dissent above is about what the control's outcome can and cannot
        distinguish, not about whether the stated arithmetic is right.

  proves_too_much_analysis:
    object_1_null_certificate:
      description: 31 frozen points plus Q=-P1; true independence count 31.
      verdict: CONCUR
      analysis: >-
        Identical object to the protocol's own null_control (see J3 finding
        3). The predicted failure signature (route must report 31, not 32)
        is FORCED by the group-homomorphism structure of Psi into an
        F2-vector space (Psi(-P)=Psi(P) always), independent of any
        implementation detail beyond correctness of the reduction map
        itself. If implemented as specified, this object cannot slip
        through: I find no configuration under which the design, correctly
        implemented, would report 32 here. This is the one place in the
        whole certificate route where the design-level guarantee is
        airtight rather than merely plausible.
    object_2_full_2_torsion_curve:
      description: >-
        Rank-0 curve with full rational 2-torsion, e.g. y^2 = x^3 - x (true
        torsion 2-rank 2, true independent-point count 0); a route reporting
        torsionRank=0 or a rank of 3 from three "independent" rows overcounts.
      verdict: DISSENT
      hand_derivation: >-
        E: y^2=x^3-x has rational 2-torsion points (0,0), (1,0), (-1,0) with
        (-1,0)=(0,0)+(1,0); E(Q)_tors is the Klein four-group (Z/2)^2,
        generated by (0,0) and (1,0) (standard, recalled fact -- this is a
        well-known CM curve, conductor 32). Reduction mod an odd prime p of
        good reduction is injective on prime-to-p torsion (Silverman AEC
        VII.3.1, recalled), so for p odd and good, (0,0) and (1,0) reduce to
        two DISTINCT nonzero 2-torsion points of E(F_p). A naive
        implementation that computes matrixRank of the two-row matrix from
        these torsion generators WITHOUT subtracting torsionRank would, for
        any p where these two reduced points' images in E(F_p)/2E(F_p) are
        F2-linearly independent (generic behavior, though not asserted here
        as guaranteed for every specific small p), report matrixRank=2 and
        (with torsionRank naively left at 0) overclaim rank 2 where the true
        rank is 0 -- exactly the review-plan's own named failure signature.
        The protocol's nearby_object_control / rational_2_torsion_applicability
        is well-aimed at this exact failure mode IN PRINCIPLE. However, per
        J2 finding 2, the document's OWN proof of "matrixRank - torsionRank
        = n implies independence" is derived ONLY for E(Q)_tors={O}; it does
        not establish, and no other part of the document establishes, that
        subtracting torsionRank is the mathematically CORRECT correction for
        a curve with nontrivial torsion (as opposed to a plausible recipe).
        So the design-level guarantee that the route "must FAIL (report the
        true, smaller number) on this object" is not yet PROVEN by anything
        in this document -- it is asserted by definition/recipe
        (controls.nearby_object_control.expected_outcome) without the
        supporting theorem. I dissent on the CLAIM that this object's correct
        rejection is design-guaranteed; I concur that the control is aimed at
        the right failure mode and would likely surface the naive bug in
        practice, which is a weaker claim than the document makes.
      required_change: >-
        Same as J2 finding 2's required change: prove the general
        (nonzero-torsion) form of matrix_rank_implies_independence_proof, or
        explicitly downgrade controls.nearby_object_control's
        expected_outcome from a proven guarantee to a design-time prediction
        pending that proof.
